subject: Regional capacity trigger & allocation framework — Nimbus AI (DEAL-8421)
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@nimbus-ai.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: deals@nimbus-ai.com
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: dedicated APAC capacity for pilot (timeline + baseline/surge)

Hi Soojin / Karthik / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Nimbus is ready to move a pilot into a dedicated environment. We need Redwood to size a dedicated APAC pool that can support our initial pilot (expected start Nov 1) and accommodate predictable growth during the quarter. High-level asks: 

- Baseline sustained QPS: 180 QPS across inference endpoints (avg payloads)
- Peak burst: up to 450 QPS for 5-10 minute spikes during batch events
- Concurrency requirement: 220 concurrent streams (chat sessions)
- Latency SLO: p95 < 220ms (APAC region)
- Data handling: no cross-region persistence; logs retained for 90d

Could you propose 2 options (conservative reserved allocation + staged tranche with burst overlay)? We need lead-time and cost delta for each. Attaching a short RFP with additional context.

Also looping in procurement (procurement@helios-procure.com) to understand contract timelines.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of Infrastructure, Nimbus AI
Attachments: Nimbus_RFP_capacity_requirements.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@nimbus-ai.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated APAC capacity for pilot (timeline + baseline/surge)

Priya — thanks, clear and helpful. Looping Soojin/Laura/Ben to lock sizing and timeline. Quick read: we can propose two practical allocation patterns tailored to your growth profile. Before I size, two quick asks: 

1) Can you share sample traffic distribution across hours (CSV) and request token distribution? That will change our batching and KV-cache planning.
2) Do you expect sustained model context length >2k tokens for the pilot? That affects GPU memory footprint.

Next steps from us: we will return 1) a conservative reserved design (capacity to meet baseline with 20% headroom) and 2) a tranche + burst overlay (smaller reserved base + burstable nodes plus pre-warmed warm-standby lanes). Each option will include: node counts (gpus), expected sustained throughput, estimated monthly cost, and lead time to provision.

Attaching a capacity template (so we can drop your CSV into it) — please populate when you can.

Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: soojin_capacity_template.xlsx

Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 11:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated APAC capacity for pilot (timeline + baseline/surge)

Karthik — thanks, attached the hour-by-hour sample and token histogram. A few clarifications:

- Traffic file has 7 days of production-mirrored load (column qps_ts, qps_value). Peak minutes listed reflect batch adaptation.
- Average request context is ~1.1k tokens, 95th at ~2.2k tokens.
- We can accept a small percentage of cold-start latency on the first minute of a burst if it reduces cost materially.

Attached: nimbus_traffic_qps.csv

Priya
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya.shah@nimbus-ai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: dedicated APAC capacity for pilot (timeline + baseline/surge)

Priya — based on the CSV and the token distribution, we ran two quick back-of-envelope configs. Summary below (see attached spreadsheet for per-node math and cost):

Option A — Reserved conservative (recommended for SLA-critical workloads)
- GPU footprint: 8 x A100-80GB equivalent nodes (sustained baseline + 20% headroom)
- Sustained throughput: ~200 QPS (meets baseline)
- Burst handling: limited; plan includes automatic routing to regional burst pool (adds latency ~30-60ms)
- Estimated lead time: 4 weeks (provision + validation)
- Estimated monthly cost (incl. infra + reserved commitment): USD 98k

Option B — Tranche + Burst overlay (cost efficient, faster to start)
- GPU footprint (reserved tranche): 4 x A100-80GB nodes
- Regional burst overlay: warm-standby 6 x smaller nodes (can scale to full capacity within 3–7 minutes)
- Sustained throughput: ~110 QPS baseline; burst to 460 QPS during events
- Estimated lead time: 2 weeks to get tranche reserved, burst overlay uses shared fleet with guaranteed backstop
- Estimated monthly cost: USD 62k (reserved commitment) + pay-for-burst usage

Operational notes / tradeoffs
- Option A gives better deterministic latency and simpler routing. Option B reduces committed spend but requires fallback tuning and modest p95 variance on bursts.
- Since you indicated p95 < 220ms, Option A is safest; Option B can meet that for baseline but may exceed p95 during the first 30–120s of large bursts.

Action items:
- If you confirm Option, we will draft a SOW and attach proposed SLAs and runbook (can be targeted to Nov 1 start if Option A and procurement signoff happens in 3 weeks).
- We recommend a 90-day pilot SOW with a baseline commit and a surge-credit clause.

Attached: proposed_allocation_v1.xlsx

Laura / Karthik — this is great, thanks for the clear choices. We will move forward with Option B (tranche + burst overlay) to limit committed spend for the pilot. A couple of procurement notes: 

- We need a short SOW and a 90-day pilot contract with surge-credit language and an exit clause. Please send your SOW draft and a DocuSign-ready contract.
- Procurement requested estimated MRR and a clear billing cadence (monthly) — we will need an itemized estimate for procurement signoff.
- Can you confirm the earliest date we can have the tranche live (not counting contract finalization)? If 2 weeks is realistic, we are aiming for Nov 1 pilot start.

If you can send the SOW + itemized estimate and the DocuSign link, we'll loop our purchasing team and get signatures moving.

Thanks,
Priya Shah
Head of Infrastructure, Nimbus AI
